questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the classes time schedules don't collide with each other. Choose courses with as many ECTS's credits as possible (6-credit courses) - because the work load doesn't align with ECTS-credits (så a 3-credit course can be as demanding as a 6-credit course = therefore choosing 6-credits courses will releive a lot of stress in the examination periode)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very demanding and in my experience the ects points did not align with the amount of work required in order to make it through

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at KU Leuven is very demanding, which the professors don't hide. They require a lot of work just to get a passing grade, and since it's the professors who decide what comes to the exams it's very important to show up to every lecture. Though, even if you do, it is sometimes still expected that you know more than what is being taught in class in the exams

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes at KU Leuven was much less interactive compared to how it's dione at UCPH. In the majoirty of the classes, the lectutres consist of the professor presenting a topic and the students listening and writing notes to whatever is being said. There are not much (if any) preparation before the classes at KU Leuven. It's the professors' words and not books that are the most important thing to pay attention to throughout the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- International Taxation
- International and European Human Rights Law
- International and European Legal Theory
- European Insurance Law
- Global Law
- European Criminal Law
- Law of World Trade Orginization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Global Law: One week intensive course, with professors from all over the world. Interesting with different perspectives, and the exam is over with quickly
- International and European Legal Theory: Has a very dedicated professor. The course gives you a different perspective on law school and the classes are much more interactive than other "traditional" law courses.

questions.answer: You were able to join the sports centre and there were many different Fakbars open every day of the week, where you could meet other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join as many social events, like the Cantuses and orientation week activities (internatonal dinner, ice-breaker events etc). That is where you will meet new people and form connections and thus built your social life

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train and visit other cities in Belgium (Ghent, Antwerpen, Brussels or Brugges). And if possible visit cities other countries that are easily accessible from Brussels (Amsterdam, Paris, Luxembourg or London)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was hard in the beginning, but after 4-6 weeks in the city, I felt at home

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was hard to navigate the everyday things, like how to recycle your trash, what to do before registering at the city hall and all of the rules regarding your living situaiton

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very open and helpful

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Show up at ALL lectures and take good notes, so you're not as stressed in the exam period (which is a VERY stressfuld period at KU Leuven)
2. Be openminded and yes to as many social happenings as you possibly can - the friends and memories are what you will remember and appreciate when you leave, and it is also those that will carry you through the tough periods in the studies
3. Don't be afraid to make friends outside of your own faculty (and definitely friends from other institutions than your home institution)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're only wanting to go on exchange to have a chill and not academically demanding semester, do NOY choose KU Leuven

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made and all the memories we created together in our spare time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To settle in in the beginning - finding a friend group and figuring out "where you belong" in this new environment
